name: Alpha-arbutin

lead: Alpha-arbutin is a synthetic glucoside of hydroquinone used in over-the-counter serums to fade dark spots and even skin tone. It is marketed as a gentler alternative to hydroquinone. The Grokipedia page covers arbutin generally, including the alpha form.
Evidence is limited: laboratory and small clinical studies support lightening activity, but high-quality controlled trials in humans are sparse.

paras: Alpha-arbutin competitively inhibits tyrosinase and slows melanin synthesis. Unlike hydroquinone, it is released slowly in the skin, which is thought to produce a milder effect with lower toxicity to melanocytes.

Side effects are generally mild, including occasional irritation. Because it can release small amounts of hydroquinone, regulators set concentration limits for cosmetic use in some regions, and effectiveness is modest compared with prescription treatments.
